events.title: Henry Hudson reaches the river that bears his name
events.description: Sailing for the Dutch East India Company, English explorer Henry Hudson reached the river that would later be named after him. He was searching for a passage to Asia.
events.significance: Hudson's voyage underpinned Dutch claims in the region. Those claims led to New Amsterdam, which later became New York City.

events.title: Louis XVI accepts the French Constitution
events.description: King Louis XVI formally accepted the new constitution drawn up during the French Revolution. The document turned absolute monarchy into a constitutional one.
events.significance: The settlement was meant to end the revolutionary upheaval. It collapsed within a year, and the monarchy was abolished in 1792.

events.title: The Great Fire of Smyrna begins
events.description: A fire broke out in the Greek and Armenian quarters of Smyrna (now Izmir) in the final phase of the Greco-Turkish War. It destroyed much of the cosmopolitan port city.
events.significance: The fire marked the end of the long Greek presence in Anatolia. It also accelerated a mass refugee crisis and the population exchange between Greece and Turkey.

events.title: Margaret Chase Smith elected to the U.S. Senate
events.description: Margaret Chase Smith of Maine won election to the U.S. Senate. She had already served in the House of Representatives.
events.significance: She became the first woman to serve in both chambers of Congress. She opened doors for later generations of women in American politics.

events.title: Lin Biao dies in a plane crash
events.description: Lin Biao was Mao Zedong's designated successor and second-in-command. He died when his plane crashed after a failed coup attempt, as he tried to flee China.
events.significance: The affair shocked China's leadership and shook faith in the Cultural Revolution. It reshaped the country's internal politics in the final years of Mao's rule.
